_doc: Studio service bench, vision slot: POST /api/services/vlm must answer 409 `provider_unavailable` — NOT 502 — while this deployment has no vision model. Measured 2026-11-02: the slot rode the platform LLM, pgx's vLLM served a text-only model (Nanbeige4.3-33B-FP8), the image part was a 400 upstream and the page told the user `The provider failed`. The provider had not failed; the deployment has no vision model. `_vlm` now refuses the PLATFORM path with SlotUnavailableError until `PROVIDER_PLATFORM_VLM_ENABLED=true` is set on a deployment that actually serves one. A TENANT vlm connection bypasses this guard and would answer 200 — this scenario pins the platform state and must be re-pointed when the capability is restored.
_expect_doc: A refusal body is the app envelope {"detail": {"code", "message"}} (routes/service_lab.py::_Refusal.response), so the assertions read detail.*, not the run fields.
_fixture_doc: An 8x8 solid grey PNG (68 base64 bytes): enough for the multipart parse and the image-type sniff, and deliberately not a real photo — this scenario asserts the REFUSAL, so the model never sees it. When a vision model is wired, replace this scenario's expectation with a 200 and give it a real image.
_cost_doc: No GPU: the guard refuses before any provider call. Still `nightly: false` — the orchestrator's schedule is removed, and this is a state assertion, not a nightly regression.
